reason: Crossing orbits can bring rocky planetesimals together, potentially starting the growth of an embryo.
expectation: I expect collisions or a growing rocky body, though some impacts might instead break material apart.

alternatives.reason: Breaking a layered body could supply fragments, but growing an embryo seems more directly tied to the goals.

effect: The impacts produced several growing embryos, so I can now pursue their further growth.
reaction: It is satisfying to see multiple embryos emerge rather than a single planet immediately.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos gather more material and grow.
expectation: I expect larger rocky embryos, though I don't know which goal this will advance.

alternatives.reason: Adding rocky planetesimals also seems useful for growth, but gravitational focusing may explain how that growth accelerates.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced an embryo that can now accrete rocky fragments.
reaction: The growth feedback is a useful explanation of why larger embryos grow faster.
reason: Adding rocky fragments seems like a direct way to grow the strongly attracting embryo.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky embryo, though I don't know whether it will be the young Earth or the other embryo.

alternatives.reason: The other embryos could also grow by gathering planetesimals, but I want to follow the strongly attracting embryo first.

effect: The fragments formed a rocky proto-Earth, which can now acquire water-bearing material.
reaction: It is satisfying to identify which embryo becomes Earth.
reason: Adding water-bearing asteroid rock directly advances the volatile-bearing young Earth goal.
expectation: I expect a young Earth containing water-bearing material, though not necessarily an ocean.

alternatives.reason: Growing another embryo also serves a goal, but I want to finish the proto-Earth route first.

effect: Proto-Earth now contains hydrated material, but that does not imply a surface ocean or complete the goal yet.
reaction: The distinction between hydrogen-bearing rock and an ocean is useful.
reason: Adding rocky planetesimals to the other embryos may advance the goal of growing another rocky embryo.
expectation: I expect another embryo to grow, though I don't know whether that will complete the goal.

alternatives.reason: Breaking the layered planetesimal might supply material for proto-Earth, but I want to advance the other embryo too.

effect: The other embryo is Theia, completing one goal; the remaining combination may provide material for proto-Earth.
reaction: Naming Theia connects the embryo to the coming impact, while acknowledging uncertainty about it.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and breaking the layered body may supply material for the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect fragments from the layered planetesimal, possibly including metal-rich material.

effect: The collision exposed metal-rich core fragments that can now be added to proto-Earth.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites makes the fragments more tangible.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may complete the volatile-bearing young Earth.
expectation: I expect proto-Earth to incorporate the metal fragments alongside its hydrated material.

effect: Adding core fragments completed the volatile-bearing young Earth; metal and hydrogen-bearing material could arrive in overlapping stages.
reaction: The uncertain timing is a useful qualification, though the final combination was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding hydrated rock was most worthwhile: it distinguished hydrogen-bearing material from a surface ocean.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final metal addition was predictable because it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: Theia emerged as the other embryo, with its exact size and composition acknowledged as uncertain.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary, although the last two combinations were the only offered actions.

continue.text: I would continue to see how Theia encounters Earth; the chapter connected that possibility to the embryos' growth while acknowledging uncertainty.
